about: LIN-3150: two independent blind hand-codings of the 220-step systematic sample drawn by scripts/survey-supervise-sample.mjs (50 steps each from Runner, leg, stepper and autopilot sessions, 20 from wakes). Codebook: action class and M (fully determined by observable state) or J (needs reading and weighing text), as defined in the codebook below. Coders: two in-session frontier-tier subagents, each coding every card without seeing the rule class or the other coder; coder 2 worked through the cards in reverse order.
codebook:
# Codebook: what does a supervisor step do? (LIN-3150)

You are hand-coding steps taken by *supervisor* sessions in Harbour, an AI-agent dispatch system. A supervisor
(passage Runner, leg, stepper, a ticket's autopilot, or a wake) does not write code itself: it dispatches worker
sessions (research, plan, review, implementation, close-out), waits for them, checks what they report, and
decides what happens next. A "step" is ONE model API message: its tool calls and/or the text it wrote.
Harbour's runner injects two recurring messages: "Your task (dispatch item X) is ready. Fetch it now" (a wake: a
child finished or reported progress) and "Before this task is marked complete, confirm its true state ... reply
with ONE sentinel line" (the completion gate; replying PENDING-EXTERNAL parks the session until the next wake).

## Classes (pick exactly ONE per step: the purpose the step exists for)
- orient — re-ground or orient: bootstrap project summary, reading the repo/docs/instructions/its own notes to find its bearings (not to check a worker's claim).
- read — read tracker or dispatch state: fetch the wake prompt, an issue, brief, relations, rulings, a child's feedback/recap/transcript.
- poll — wait or poll: CI, PR state, child status; acknowledging a progress-only wake that changes nothing.
- judge — judge a worker's report: spot-check its claims against the repo or tracker; accept it, route it back or escalate it.
- decide — decide the next task or design question: ask the engine (recommend) what is next, weigh options, choose.
- dispatch — dispatch the next phase or beat: write the worker prompt and/or send it.
- relay — relay a ruling or escalation: put a decision to John (BLOCKED/DECISION), or pass a ruling/verdict on to another session or ticket.
- rearm — re-arm a wake: answer the completion gate with a PENDING sentinel, schedule a wake, arm a monitor.
- restate — restate or summarise state: a progress report to the operator, a status comment, a note in its own state file.
- land — act on the record: set status or labels, merge a PR, mark Done.
- work — do a worker's job itself: edit code/docs/tests in the repo, commit or push.
- recover — recover from an error: retry or work around a failed call.

## Mechanical or judgement (one per step)
- M — mechanical: what the step did was FULLY determined by observable state — a status, a label, a CI result, a
  verdict string, a dispatch id, a sentinel format, a fixed template. A short deterministic program with access to
  the same APIs could have produced an equivalent action. Fetching a known URL, answering the gate with
  "PENDING-EXTERNAL: waiting on <the child it just dispatched>", acknowledging a progress-only wake, appending a
  status line to a state file, re-sending a recommended prompt verbatim — all M.
- J — judgement: the step had to read and weigh free text (a worker's recap, a diff, a plan, a review finding, a
  ruling) and its action depends on that weighing — e.g. deciding a beat's claims hold or do not, choosing which of
  several options to take, writing a beat prompt that carries corrections or new scope, drafting an escalation
  that frames a decision. Writing prose is not by itself J: a summary that only restates statuses is M.
When a step looks mixed, code what the step's ACTION depended on. If you cannot tell from the card, choose the
more conservative J and say so in the note.

## Failure flag (optional)
If the card itself shows a supervisor mistake — routing to the wrong phase/ticket, a missed or duplicate wake,
repeating the same action in a loop, doing a worker's job (leaving altitude), a wrong claim about state — set
"fail" to a few words. Otherwise omit it.

## Output
Write a JSON array to the output file you are given, one object per card, in card order:
{"id": "<ID from the card>", "cls": "<class>", "mj": "M" | "J", "note": "<≤15 words, why>", "fail": "<optional>"}
Code every card. Work independently: do not look for other coders' files, and do not read any file under the
LinearViewer repo's scripts/ or data/ directories other than your card file.
